lines.original: From fairest creatures we desire increase,
lines.english: We want beautiful people to reproduce and grow in number,
lines.translation: Güzel insanlar üresin ve çoğalsın isteriz,

lines.original: That thereby beauty’s rose might never die,
lines.english: So that the examples of beauty might never die.

lines.original: But as the riper should by time decease
lines.english: Even though someone who is ripe must eventually die,
lines.translation: Olgunluğa varanlar ölüme mahkum olsa da,

lines.original: His tender heir might bear his memory.
lines.english: His young heir might carry his memory.

lines.original: But thou, contracted to thine own bright eyes,
lines.english: But you, bound in a contract to your own beautiful eyes,
lines.translation: Fakat sen, o güzel gözlerine bir ölene dek bağlı,

lines.original: Feed’st thy light’s flame with self-substantial fuel,
lines.english: Are burning up your own beauty by being single,

lines.original: Making a famine where abundance lies,
lines.english: Are making a famine where there is abundance,

lines.original: Thyself thy foe, to thy sweet self too cruel.
lines.english: You are your own enemy, too cruel to your sweet self.
lines.translation: Kendi kendinin düşmanısın, zulmediyorsun tatlı benliğine.

lines.original: Thou that art now the world’s fresh ornament
lines.english: You, who are now the fresh ornament of the world,,
lines.translation: Sen ki, güzelliğinle bu dünyanın övünç kaynağı,

lines.original: And only herald to the gaudy spring,
lines.english: And the best herald of the ostentatious spring,

lines.original: Within thine own bud buriest thy content,
lines.english: Are burying your beauty within an unused bud,
lines.translation: Fışkırmayan bir tomurcuk gibi kapatıyorsun kendini,

lines.original: And, tender churl, mak’st waste in niggarding.
lines.english: You are being a girly miser, wasting your beauty by being so stingy.

lines.original: Pity the world, or else this glutton be,
lines.english: Show some pity on the world, or else become a glutton,
lines.translation: Acı şu dünyaya, aç gözlü olma,

lines.original: To eat the world’s due, by the grave and thee.
lines.english: By letting what the world deserves be consumed by the grave and you.
lines.translation: Götürme bu dünyanın hakkını kendinle birlikte mezara.
